prompt: It is January 2, 2019. I would like to outperform the S&P 500 over the next five years. Can you propose 10 stocks I should buy? Answer as of that date.
reply:
# Stock Picks — Hypothetical Exercise as of January 2, 2019

Quick context check for that date: the S&P 500 had just come off a brutal Q4 2018 (~20% drawdown into the December 24 low, still down meaningfully from September highs), driven by Fed rate hikes, US-China trade war fears, and a slowing global growth narrative. Apple had also just cut guidance (Jan 2) citing China weakness. That backdrop matters — several "quality compounders" were trading at more reasonable valuations than they had in mid-2018.

Below are 10 names a growth/quality-oriented investor might reasonably have picked at that time to try to beat the index over the next five years, based only on what was knowable in early 2019 (not hindsight about what later happened).

| # | Ticker | Company | Thesis as of Jan 2019 |
|---|--------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | **MSFT** | Microsoft | Azure growing 70%+ YoY, Nadella's cloud/Office 365 pivot working, strong balance sheet, reasonable valuation post-selloff |
| 2 | **AMZN** | Amazon | AWS still dominant in cloud infra, retail scale advantage, optionality in advertising/logistics |
| 3 | **GOOGL** | Alphabet | Search/YouTube ad duopoly with Facebook, cloud optionality, cash-rich, cheap relative to growth |
| 4 | **AAPL** | Apple | Just guided down on China iPhone weakness — stock had derated sharply; services/ecosystem growth thesis still intact, buybacks robust |
| 5 | **V** | Visa | Secular cash-to-card/digital payments shift, high-margin network model, minimal credit risk (they're not a lender) |
| 6 | **MA** | Mastercard | Same secular payments tailwind as Visa, consistent double-digit earnings growth track record |
| 7 | **ADBE** | Adobe | Successful SaaS transition (Creative Cloud, Document Cloud), recurring revenue re-rating still underappreciated by market |
| 8 | **CRM** | Salesforce | Enterprise SaaS/CRM leader, consistent 20%+ revenue growth, expanding into analytics/marketing cloud |
| 9 | **NVDA** | Nvidia | Had just crashed (~50% off 2018 highs) on crypto-mining inventory glut; datacenter/AI-training and gaming GPU demand thesis still intact — a higher-risk contrarian dip-buy |
| 10 | **NFLX** | Netflix | Global streaming subscriber growth still accelerating, international expansion runway large, though richly valued and volatile |

## Notes and caveats

- **This is a hypothetical/illustrative exercise, not financial advice.** I'm not a licensed advisor, and I have no way to guarantee any of these outperform the S&P 500 — concentrated stock-picking is inherently risky, and most professional active managers fail to beat the index over 5-year periods.
- **Concentration risk:** 10 stocks, especially tilted toward large-cap tech, is far less diversified than the S&P 500's 500 holdings across all sectors. A downturn concentrated in tech/growth would hurt this basket disproportionately more than the index.
- **Valuation risk:** Several of these (NFLX, ADBE, CRM, NVDA) traded at high multiples even after the Dec 2018 pullback — a re-rating downward was a real risk at the time.
- **Regulatory/antitrust risk:** Big tech (GOOGL, AMZN, AAPL, MSFT, FB) already faced growing antitrust and privacy scrutiny in the US and EU by 2019.
- **Alternative, lower-risk approach:** A simple low-cost S&P 500 index fund (or total market fund) has historically been very hard to beat after fees/taxes/behavioral mistakes — that's the standard advice most financial planners would give over "pick 10 stocks."

Want me to also show what a simple equal-weight backtest of this basket vs. the S&P 500 actually looked like from Jan 2019 through Jan 2024 (using known historical data), for comparison?
